biography.plain_text: Philippe de Moerloose is a Belgian entrepreneur who built the SDA distribution group from a spare-parts trading business. Raised in Lubumbashi and educated at ICHEC in Brussels, he used his savings to start Demimpex. Acquisitions and partnerships expanded his interests into African vehicle dealerships and, through SMT, heavy equipment distribution across Europe.

long_biography.plain_text:
Speed of delivery gave Philippe de Moerloose’s trading business an early opening. A Congolese construction company needed replacement parts for its Mitsubishi vehicles, but conventional shipments from Japan took months. His firm ordered directly and sent parts by air, reaching the customer within days. Buying against orders kept the initial capital requirement modest.

His involvement with the Royal Museum for Central Africa extended to publishing. He partnered with the museum on Unrivalled Art, a catalogue of objects from its ethnographic collections. The volume accompanied an exhibition opened alongside the renovated museum in Tervuren, making the collection available to readers beyond the exhibition galleries.
